name: wait_for_workstream
description: Block until one or all named child workstreams reach a terminal state. Prefer this over busy-polling inspect_workstream after a fan-out - one call + one result regardless of duration. Real terminal states: `idle`, `error`, `closed`, `deleted` (unobservable - hard-delete cascades the row out of storage). Returns `{results: {ws_id: {state, tokens, updated, name, message, truncated}}, elapsed, complete, mode}`; `complete` = the wait condition fired before timeout. `message` is non-null only on real-terminal rows (child's last assistant text for idle/error, a short sentinel for closed/not_found), capped at 10 KiB UTF-8 with `truncated=true` when capped - re-read via inspect_workstream. Ids are validated up front - copy them VERBATIM from spawn_batch/list_workstreams results. A malformed id errors immediately with `did_you_mean` suggestions and your children roster; an unobservable id (foreign / nonexistent / hard-deleted mid-wait) aborts the wait on the tick that sees it with `state='not_found'` plus top-level `error`/`not_found`/`children`. When that happens fix the id and re-issue - do NOT assume the child is dead. Child display names are labels, not addresses; always target ids. Caps: 32 ws_ids, 600s - over-cap errors rather than truncating.

ws_ids.description: Workstream ids to wait on (each exactly 32 hex chars, copied verbatim from spawn_batch / list_workstreams results). Accepts 1 or more; capped at 32 per call. Malformed ids fail the call before any waiting; well-formed ids that can't be observed abort it on the first tick - both return did-you-mean suggestions.

timeout.description: Maximum seconds to block, capped at 600. Default 60 - for longer waits, call again with the same ws_ids.

mode.description: 'any' (default) returns when the first child reaches a real terminal state (`idle` / `error` / `closed` / `deleted`); 'all' once every named child is real-terminal. An unobservable id (foreign / nonexistent / deleted mid-wait) aborts the wait immediately with state='not_found' and a top-level error, regardless of mode.

since.description: Optional prior snapshot (typically the `results` dict from an earlier call): the wait exits early when ANY polled ws_id having a `since` entry differs from it (state/tokens/updated), regardless of mode - skips re-counting already-terminal children on follow-up waits. Ids absent from `since` fall back to the normal `mode` condition, so a disjoint `since` dict never exits on tick one. Omit for default terminal-state behavior.
